CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Lawrence is a 62-year-old male who presents with complaints of shortness of breath and swelling. Patient attributes symptoms to recent attendance at house parties with consumption of salty foods. He reports feeling lethargic. Shortness of breath is exertional, occurring with walking up stairs. Symptoms have been present for approximately 10 days. Patient reports some leg swelling. He notes discomfort lying flat in bed and stiffness upon waking in the morning that takes time to resolve with walking. He had one episode of acute shortness of breath at night approximately one week ago but has not had recurrence since and is not overly concerned about this. Denies recent spike in blood sugars despite not consistently monitoring on weekends.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorsed shortness of breath on review of systems sheet completed at check-in. Denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, or abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 1 diabetes
Congestive heart failure
Depression
Reflux

MEDICATIONS
Insulin pump
Omeprazole

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports regular consumption of chocolate bars. Eats salty foods when attending house parties. Monitors blood glucose regularly during work week but forgets on weekends due to being busy. Previously doing morning stretches outdoors during summer to help manage depression but has stopped with weather change. Has tried natural solutions for depression but is not yet ready to try medications. Reports cutting back on Red Bull and caffeine. Alcohol intake has been difficult during holiday season but is improving.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Good
Pulse oximetry: Good
Neck: No jugular venous distension, no carotid bruits
Heart: Slight 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur
Lungs: Crackles bilaterally at bases
Lower extremities: 1+ pitting edema

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No evidence of airspace disease
Labs: No elevated white blood cell count, no pneumonia

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute heart failure exacerbation: Start Lasix 40 mg daily. Patient to weigh self daily. Call if weight not decreasing or increasing. Call or go to emergency room if shortness of breath worsens at rest; may need IV diuretics.

2. Type 1 diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1c in approximately one month to assess for needed adjustments. Follow up with endocrinologist. Ensure recent eye exam.

3. Depression: Refer to psychiatry for talk therapy. No medications at this time.

4. Reflux: Continue omeprazole 20 mg daily.
